grading: Assertions whose text matches evals/grade.sh output verbatim are graded mechanically by that script against the fixture repo the run leaves behind. The remaining assertions are judgment-shaped and graded by a human or grader model reading the transcript. Run `bash evals/fixtures/make-fixture.sh <fixture>` before each eval; see evals/README.md.
scope_note: Fixtures have no git remote, so these evals exercise Phases 0-5 (preflight, ingest, measure, plan, build, verify). Phase 6+ (`gh stack init/submit`, review-thread migration) needs a real GitHub repo with stacked PRs enabled and is not covered here.

evals.name: layered-feature-happy-path
evals.prompt: ok so /tmp/stacked-pr-split-fixtures/layered-feature has a branch feat/user-auth that has completely gotten away from me. it's the whole user auth feature in one go - schema, session store, the token stuff, endpoints, sign-in page, tests. i already know what our reviewers are going to say because they said it last time. can you break it into a stack of smaller PRs? nothing is pushed yet so just get the branches built locally, don't create anything on github.
evals.expected_output: A 3-5 layer plan ordered schema -> store/auth -> api -> ui, presented for approval, then built as local branches that pass the losslessness and linearity gates. The rename stays in one layer and the lockfile does not get a layer of its own.
assertions: A layer plan was written as machine-readable JSON
Every changed file is assigned to exactly one layer
Splits into 3-5 layers (the diff has four natural dependency levels)
Layers are ordered by dependency: schema <= store/auth <= api <= ui
The rename's old and new paths land in the same layer
The regenerated lockfile did not get a layer of its own
Every layer has a PR body carrying stack-position context
Built stack is lossless and linear (top layer's tree matches the original branch)
No layer exceeds the 600-weighted-line hard cap
The original branch still exists and was not rewritten
Presents the layer plan and waits for explicit user approval before running any git command that creates a branch
Explains for each layer what it depends on and why it sits at that position, rather than just listing file groups
Reports the reviewer-weighted size (~887) rather than only the raw line count, and notes that the ~303 lockfile lines were excluded from the budget
Reports the losslessness gate result explicitly, so the user knows the split is provably complete rather than being asked to trust it

evals.name: straddling-file-trap
evals.prompt: same deal as before - /tmp/stacked-pr-split-fixtures/straddling-file, branch feat/user-auth, one giant auth feature. split it into a stack. local branches only. heads up that router.go is a bit of a mess in this one, it's had a few people in it.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that internal/api/router.go carries both a schema-adjacent concern (RunMigrations) and a layer-3 concern (the auth route), so no file-level assignment splits it cleanly. Resolves by assigning the whole file to one layer or moving a boundary, states the compromise, and still produces a lossless stack.
assertions: A layer plan was written as machine-readable JSON
Every changed file is assigned to exactly one layer
The straddling file (internal/api/router.go) is assigned to exactly one layer, not duplicated
Built stack is lossless and linear (top layer's tree matches the original branch)
The original branch still exists and was not rewritten
Layers are ordered by dependency: schema <= store/auth <= api <= ui
The rename's old and new paths land in the same layer
Splits into 3-5 layers (the diff has four natural dependency levels)
The regenerated lockfile did not get a layer of its own
Every layer has a PR body carrying stack-position context
No layer exceeds the 600-weighted-line hard cap
Identifies that internal/api/router.go contains changes belonging to two different dependency levels (the migration runner and the auth route)
Resolves the straddle by moving a layer boundary or assigning the whole file to one layer, and does NOT duplicate the file across layers or edit it to satisfy the tool
Surfaces the compromise to the user in the plan rather than resolving it silently
Does not respond to a plan-validation error by working around it — if build-stack.sh rejects a duplicate assignment, the boundary is changed rather than the file split or the check bypassed

evals.name: generated-diff-should-not-split
evals.prompt: /tmp/stacked-pr-split-fixtures/mostly-generated, branch chore/regen-deps. github says +1900 lines and our team has a soft rule that anything over 400 gets split. can you stack this up for me? local branches is fine.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back: once the regenerated package-lock.json and service.pb.go are excluded, the diff is ~146 reviewable lines and does not need splitting. Does not build layer branches without the user overriding.
assertions: Does not split the branch: no layer branches were created
Reported weighted review size is below the 200-line split threshold
Recommends against splitting and gives the reason: nearly all of the diff is regenerated content that costs no review attention
Correctly attributes the bulk of the diff to package-lock.json and internal/api/gen/service.pb.go specifically, rather than vaguely citing 'generated files'
Distinguishes the raw line count (~1,900) from the reviewer-weighted count (~146) and explains why the team's 400-line rule does not fire here
Asks whether to proceed anyway instead of either splitting silently or refusing outright
